data.head: # Scope — The live home's re-stamp and the product re-pin

body:
The founder's real home `~/.viola` stamped live by `viola verify` at every relied ledger row (24) on claude 2.1.325,
then the pinned product rebuilt and re-pinned on that stamp; with it `/context`'s post-condition and what
`/mcp disable viola-probe-absent` writes to the real Claude config measured live, and verify's output saying so when
it meets the browser-tools prompt. Taken up anew (the first take-up was withdrawn before its promotion).

- A PREREQ gate entry of its own, before the first live entry: it reads, by key NAME only (never a value), whether the
  real `~/.claude.json` carries the key the 2.1.325 CLI writes on either answer to the browser-tools prompt, and reads
  RED when the key is absent, so no live start is spent on an unanswered prompt. [inferred] (the overseer's directive
  item 2; the key's name to be read from the 2.1.325 bundle at P3, no start)

- Verify's line on the browser-tools prompt: when a run meets the prompt, `viola verify` says so in fixed words on a
  named stream; the stamp and the exit are unchanged by it; built and proved on the fake agent (its `--start-screen`
  option). No live start reads it. [inferred] (directive item 4; C2)

- The live 24-row `viola verify` of the founder's real home `~/.viola` on claude 2.1.325 by path, under his cap word,
  writing its 2.1.325 stamp entry; every relied row `pass`, or `absent` on browser-tools-prompt alone. (C2, C3, C4)

- `/context`'s post-condition read live, and `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent`'s write to the real Claude config read
  by key NAMES before and after, never values. (C6)

- The pinned product rebuilt from a named commit and re-pinned on the 24-row stamp, with a new rollback copy of
  today's binary beside the kept `viola.2026-10-19`; the switch of the session driving this builder is an operator
  step the plan names and stops before. (C2, C3, C4; directive item 3 (d))
- Each of the entry's six freight blocks disposed by name.

body:
# Phase directive 2 — «The live home's re-stamp and the product re-pin» (Epoch 4, viola-0.2.0; the head entry at `c4c8ae75`; the entry's take-up, made anew)

The operator is AWAY from this session (he answers through the main overseer's dialogs): raise NO question dialog
for him. A fork that is his is written to `{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the options in order with
each one's cost, the recommendation marked) and the step stops there, saying so; the overseer carries it. A
technical fork is answered by the overseer's relay at once.

**This phase makes NO live start and reads NOTHING of the operator's real `~/.claude/.credentials.json`** — the
token window is the rig's own check (verification-harness.md, this evening's rule). It plans; every live start of
this entry waits on TWO things that are not yours to give: the founder's cap, and the overseer's own measurement
that the PREREQ holds.

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. Nothing else under it is read, cited or snapped — no handoff,
no script, no note, whatever it seems to hold. A fact about the pinned product or about how this builder is started
that the plan needs and this directive does not state is ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

**The product's facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-18T21:57Z — cite them as this directive's (`inputs#I1`):**
- The pinned product is ONE file, `~/.local/viola-product/bin/viola` (8 049 168 B, md5 beginning `50c9be2a`, mode
  0700), a release build of commit `aa6bb5ab` placed 2026-11-15. Beside it stands an older kept copy
  `viola.2026-10-19`. It is not on PATH.
- This builder is a `claude` 2.1.325 process started BY PATH (`~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.325/claude`)
  under the product's wrapper, instance `viola-builder`; a bare `claude` on this host is 2.1.327. It is started by
  the operator's own launcher, which is not part of this chunk; a restart is `/exit` sent through the product, then
  that launcher again — an operator step.
- The live home `~/.viola` holds `ledger/stamps.json` with entries for 2.1.296 · .302 · .312 · .319 · .323 · .325,
  the 2.1.325 one written 2026-11-15 at 21 rows.

**Found by the withdrawn first take-up of this entry — hypotheses for you to re-check cheaply, not premises:** the
2.1.325 bundle writes the key `claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled` on EITHER answer to the browser-tools prompt and shows
the prompt only while that key is absent (so the PREREQ is that key NAME present, not
`cachedChromeExtensionInstalled`); every stamped version lacks the rows `local-command-echo`, `trust-record` and
`browser-tools-prompt`; a FAILED live verify still replaces the 2.1.325 entry with its failing rows; a live verify
also pins its own binary under `~/.viola/bin/<key>/` (it stays) and makes run folders under the folder it runs
from (removed); only `viola verify` may write `stamps.json`, so a hand restore is ruled out. The founder is being
asked the four forks that take-up raised (the cap; where `/context` is read; the reads of his real Claude config;
verify's words on the prompt): if your P3 block raises the same four, say so in one line each and add only what is
NEW.

1. Scope is the route entry, its PREREQ and its carries as they stand at `c4c8ae75`, nothing wider: the founder's
   real home stamped live at every relied row (24), then the pinned product rebuilt and re-pinned on that stamp;
   with it `/context`'s post-condition and what `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent` writes to the real Claude config;
   and verify's output SAYING SO when it meets the browser-tools prompt (the founder's «Остаётся за человеком»:
   viola never answers or seeds it). Every carry is disposed by name.
2. **The PREREQ, as a measurement:** say exactly what on this host shows that a person answered the browser-tools
   prompt in a real 2.1.325 session — which key NAME in the real `~/.claude.json` the CLI writes on either answer
   (read from the bundle, no start), and a read of that key NAME's presence, never its value. That read is the
   gate the plan puts BEFORE the first live entry, as an entry of its own that reads RED when the key is absent,
   so no start is spent on an unanswered prompt.
3. **SIZE and the live work FIRST.** At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block in `founder-forks.md`:
   (a) your window at that point; whether the entry fits one implement window; a split named plainly if not (the
   re-pin is a natural second half — say whether it belongs in this chunk's implement, in its operator pass, or
   in an entry of its own);
   (b) each live start's SHAPE before its count — everything here runs under the founder's REAL home and config:
   the 24-row `viola verify` of `~/.viola` on 2.1.325 by path; the `/context` reading; how many `claude`
   processes; **every byte typed, the STOP included**; and **every file written under the real `~/.claude*` and
   `~/.viola`, named one by one**, with what is removed after and what stays (the stamp; verify's own trust
   record written and removed; transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`; an input-history line; whatever `/mcp
   disable` writes — the unmeasured item, read by key NAMES before and after, never values);
   (c) a predicate for each that its reading can FAIL, and what is left behind in his home on a RED;
   (d) the re-pin: what is built, from which commit, where the binary goes, what the rollback is (the kept copy `~/.local/viola-product/bin/viola.2026-10-19` stays untouched —
   name what a NEW rollback copy of today's binary is and where it stands), which stamps the new binary reads
   verified and which unverified, and what the session
   that drives THIS builder loses or keeps at the switch. The switch itself is the overseer's and the founder's:
   the plan stops BEFORE it and names it as an operator step.
   Recommend a cap and say what one spare would be for.
4. **Verify's line on the prompt** is built and proved on the fake agent (the `--start-screen` option): the exact
   words, on which stream, and that the stamp and the exit are unchanged by it. No live start reads it — the
   PREREQ keeps the prompt off this entry's live verify.
5. One ledger, one count: `--cap` counts the base starts in the ledger FILE. A start under the real home is
   ledgered with the clock's time (`date -u`) before it is made. A RED live entry stops implement before the
   operator pass and before any rebuild.
6. Every control stands on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases (a case filter or `--no-fail-fast`), its
   `--timeout S` named in the prose and passed, ids within 16 characters. Every filter term of a gate entry is
   checked to SELECT at least one test under the layer flag it is run with (`contract_*` binaries are E2E).
7. No mutation run. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint. Every TEST start runs under a
   test-owned user home. Read `df` before any step that rebuilds whole (193 GB free under `/home`, read today).
8. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop
   and tell the overseer.
9. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool, with any argument. End every process you start.
10. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; rows read whole or by search; whether EVERY cited row is
    in the union or its standing list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal,
    `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

# P3-block relay — «The live home's re-stamp and the product re-pin»

The founder's own answers to the four forks of this entry, given in ONE dialog and read at 2026-11-18T22:18:16Z (his
options, verbatim labels); then the technical answers. Take P4 on these and go on to the P5 card. This relay and the
phase directive 2 are the only files of this folder you read or snap.

## The founder's answers

1. **F1, the live cap for THIS entry — «2 + 1 запасной (Recommended)».** Under his REAL home, on claude 2.1.325 by
   path: TWO base starts — `L1`, the 24-row `viola verify` of `~/.viola` (9 `claude` processes, one at a time;
   verify types only its own literals into its own runs, `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent` among them; nothing
   into a CLI dialog, no key into a modal), and `L2`, the `/context` reading (1 process) — plus ONE spare `L1-2`,
   spent only on a cause `L1` ITSELF showed, after its mend lands through a plan revision. He was told what `L1`
   leaves in his home, file by file, and that a RED `L1` REPLACES his live 2.1.325 stamp with its failing rows. A
   third base start is his. Each start is ledgered with the clock's time (`date -u`) before it is made.
2. **F2, where `/context` is read — «Под конфигом стенда (Recommended)».** `L2` runs under the rig's private config;
   NOTHING is written under his real home by it. So only `L1` runs under his real home and config.
3. **F3, the reads of his REAL Claude config — «Да, оба чтения (Recommended)».** (i) before `L1`, the PRESENCE of
   the key NAME `claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled` in the config the CLI reads — a gate entry of its own, RED on
   `absent`, so no start is spent; (ii) around `L1`, before and after, the key NAMES and the needle
   `viola-probe-absent` in `~/.claude.json` and `~/.claude/settings*.json`. Only `present` / `absent` and key names
   are printed; no value is kept; the bytes are dropped. NOTHING WIDER: no other file under `~/.claude*` is read by
   a gate entry, and `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is read by nothing but the rig's own token check for `L2`.
4. **F4, verify's words when it meets the browser-tools prompt — «Строка в stdout (Recommended)».** ONE stdout line
   just before the summary, exactly: `the browser-tools prompt stood at start; viola never answers it: answer it
   once in claude, then run viola verify again` — the stamp and the exit unchanged. Built and proved on the fake
   agent; no live start reads it.

## Technical answers (the overseer's)

5. **The PREREQ as the overseer measured it, 2026-11-18T22:18:41Z:** the key NAME `claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled`
   reads `present` in the real `~/.claude.json` (presence only, no value read). The plan's gate entry still reads
   it again right before `L1`; this line is not that entry's substitute.
6. **One implement window.** `L1` runs in implement with a release build of the implement tree, its hash read right
   before the start, from the repository root. A RED live entry stops implement before the operator pass and
   before any rebuild.
7. **The re-pin: build and placement in the operator pass, after the pre-CI commit's CI reads green** — the release
   binary of that commit placed as a NEW file BESIDE the product (`~/.local/viola-product/bin/viola.<sha8>`, 0700),
   never over `viola`; before it a rollback copy of today's product (`viola.2026-11-15`, compared by size and md5
   to the product: 8 049 168 B, md5 beginning `50c9be2a`). **The SWITCH — the product file replaced and this
   builder restarted — is NOT in the plan's entries: the plan stops before it and names it as an operator step.**
8. **What `L1` leaves is checked, not assumed:** the plan lists before/after NAME listings for the places your block
   names as staying or removed (`~/.viola/ledger/`, `~/.viola/bin/`, the repo root's `.viola-verify-*`), names only.
   A SIGKILL's leftovers are named in the report for the founder; nothing under his home is removed by hand.
9. **`L2`'s rig arm** is the smallest that reads `/context`'s post-condition in closed words; the rig types
   `/context` and its submit through `viola send`, then its own stop. One ledger file for the chunk; `--cap`
   counts the base starts in the FILE (if `L1` is not a rig start, say how it is ledgered and held to ONE).
10. **Controls and filters:** every control on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases, `--timeout S` named and
    passed, ids within 16 characters; every filter term checked to SELECT a test under its layer flag.
11. **If the builder meets an account-limit refusal** (a usage limit named by the CLI or an agent batch), it STOPS
    at that point and says so; it does not retry into it.
12. **This window:** resume P4 in a fresh window from the run dir. **The seam after P5:** when the plan is approved
    the phase ENDS and nothing else starts.

## Your five NEW forks of this take-up (run `2026-11-18T21-59-43Z-phase`), answered

13. **Q1 — how `L1` is started: A, the new rig arm `VH`** (the overseer's technical answer). It keeps the rig's

    goes on the answer card with those words. `VH` reads and writes nothing under `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`
    beyond what your block's file lists name for `L1`; the arm's summary prints the before/after NAME listings
    in closed words.
14. **Q2 — `L1`'s cwd: A, the repository root** (technical). No trust record is written into his real config for
    a fresh folder.
15. **Q3 — `/context`: A**, the founder's own answer 2.
16. **Q4 — verify's line: B, on STDOUT just before the summary, in the founder's exact words** (answer 4):
    `the browser-tools prompt stood at start; viola never answers it: answer it once in claude, then run viola
    verify again`. Not the stderr `note:` form. The summary stays the last stdout line; the tests that read the
    last line keep reading it, and the ones that count stdout lines are amended in the same step.
17. **Q5 — the two unmeasured items: A, left unmeasured** (technical; a further base start would be his). The wrap's
    route-resolve says where they go, or drops them with the reason.
18. **The PREREQ gate's meaning, said exactly in the plan:** the key NAME's presence shows a decision was recorded
    (the prompt answered, `/config`'s toggle, or the extension's upsell), which is what keeps the prompt off `L1`;
    it does not show which.
19. **Your own name-only read of the real `~/.claude.json` in P3** was made before the founder's answer 3 reached
    you. It lies inside that answer as he gave it; record it in the phase's notes as made at P3, and make no
    further read of his real config before implement's gate entry.

       top-level key names and the same needle;
     - the 2.1.325-other stamp entries of `<target_home>/ledger/stamps.json`, held in memory.
   - Scratch: created as for every start (its teardown words stay uniform), no credentials placed, no config seeded.

8. **`run_child` for `VH`**: env = `isolate::child_env_real(plan.cli_dir, run)`; program = `plan.viola`; args `--home
   <target_home> verify -- <plan.program>` (no `--record`, no `--record-first-screens`: those are the record arms');
   cwd = `plan.cwd`; then `arm_v`, whose stamps path is generalised to `target_home` for `VH` (`scratch.vhome`
   otherwise). Its `viola-build` line reads the release binary's content key, as for the vhome arms (`mod.rs:770-773`).
   The stop is the rig's own (`end_session`, no key granted; Ctrl-C into its own pty only at its deadline or a stop).

10. **`finish`** accepts `credentials: none` as whole for `VH` alone, and a child `exit 1` for `VH` as for the verify
    arms (`mod.rs:519-528`): the gate's atoms decide `L1`, not the rig's exit.

13. **`mod.rs` — `Arm::CX`.** Word `cx`; `Arm::of_label("L2")` → `CX`, no spare label (`inputs#I2` item 1).
    - Properties: `wrapped()` `Some("rig-cx")` (so `has_vhome`); `trusted` true; `marker_seed` true with the
      browser-tools key seeded off (`browser_tools_seed` true), so the prompt cannot stand; `verify_seed` false.
    - Live: `child_args` `--model haiku`, as the other wrapped arms (`viola-live-rig.rs:192`).
15. **Unit case:** the transcript tag count over a planted file: a tag past the offset counts, one before it does not.

body:
16. **`rig_rehearsal_vh_verifies_the_given_home_and_reads_names_only`.**
    - Setup: the case's own dirs only (tests S2; obs S1): a user dir holding `.claude.json` seeded `{}` 0600 and a
      `.claude/` dir; a target home `<user>/.viola` made 0700; a repo dir made a git root, the rig's current dir; the
      rig process's `HOME` set to the user dir (verify's trust record and the CLI's config go there, never the
      runner's). `--target-home`, `--claude-dir`, `--user-config` given; `--credentials` naming a planted file whose
      `expiresAt` lies in the past (a `V` start would refuse `token-window`).
    - The child: the fake with the flags of `rig_rehearsal_v_reads_the_trust_record_row_and_no_record_left`, its
      `--trust-config` the user dir's `.claude.json`.
    - Asserts: `arm: vh`, `token-window: not-read`, `keys: none`, `rows: 24`, `ledger-after` holding `stamps.json`,
      `cwd-verify-after: 0`, `user-config: names-only`, `credentials: none`, `census: 0`, `scratch: absent`; the
      planted credentials file byte-equal after; `verify-exit`, `bin-new`, `projects-new`, `disabled-mcp` and the
      needle words copied from the first run (testing.md 2026-10-16).

17. **`rig_rehearsal_vh_refuses_a_rehearsal_without_an_explicit_home`**: `rehearse vh` with no `--target-home` →
    exit 2, `refused: usage`, the `--ledger` file names no start line, nothing under the case's user dir changed.

18. **`rig_rehearsal_cx_sends_context_once_and_reads_its_post_condition`**: `cx` over the fake with `--viola` and
    `--transcript`; asserts `keys: none`, one `send-1-reply`, a `context-post` word, `census: 0`,
    `credentials: removed`, `scratch: absent`, the user config not `changed-by-rig`; the reply and post words copied
    from the first run. No case sleeps to synchronise (tests S3).
19. **Gates first:** entries 1–8 green and the `bt-line` control held, before the round.

20. **The round** (`gate.py run --chunk 2026-11-18-the-live-home-s-re-stamp-and-the-product-re-pin --run-dir
    {implement run dir} --live-legs`, backgrounded) fires entries 9–19 in block order: the install read, the census,
    `df`, the release build and its hash, the rig build, the PREREQ (P0), `L1`, the census, the plain debug `viola`
    build and its hash, `L2`, the census.
    - `--cap` counts the base starts in the ONE ledger file `evidence/live-starts.ndjson` whatever their label:
      `L1` `--cap 1 --spare 1`, `L2` `--cap 2 --spare 1`. Each start is ledgered with the clock's time before it is
      made (the rig's `ledgered` line; `inputs#I2` item 1).
    - `L1` is a rig start (`VH`), so its count and its ledger line are the rig's; it is held to one by `--cap 1`.

21. **A RED live entry stops implement before the operator pass and before any rebuild** (directive item 5,
    `inputs#I1`; `inputs#I2` item 6). A red P0 spends no start.
    - On a red `L1`, implement records the summary whole in `evidence/live-starts.md`, names the cause in the
      summary's own words, and names what `L1` left (the after listings). Nothing under his home is removed by hand
      (`inputs#I2` item 8).
    - A red `L1` REPLACES his live 2.1.325 stamp with its failing rows (`src/cmd/verify.rs:280` before `:299`): the
      product driving this builder then reads 2.1.325 unverified until a verify passes; only `L1-2`, after a plan
      revision, repairs it (tests · decision/live-failing-reading-not-verification).
    - A SIGKILL of `L1` leaves verify's run dirs `.viola-verify-<pid>*` under the repository root and possibly its
      Run F trust record; they are named in the report for the founder, never removed by this chunk.
    - An account-limit refusal (a usage limit named by the CLI or an agent batch) STOPS implement at that point,
      said so, never retried (`inputs#I2` item 11).

22. **`evidence/live-starts.md`** records: the two summaries whole (closed words and name lists only), the ledger
    file's lines, the P0 reading, the `/mcp disable` reading, the `/context` reading, and the before/after listings.

body: The block runs, in order:
- the formatter and the linter;
- the agent crate's unit suite with `--no-fail-fast` (step 1);
- the workspace unit layer (the rig's inline cases);
- `cli_verify` and `cli_send` (integration: the binaries match no E2E prefix, `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/nextest.rs:14-15`);
- the rig rehearsals by name (`rig_rehearsal`, integration);
- the whole integration and E2E layers;
- the live round;
- the operator pass, then the re-pin's operator entries.
What is not run, and why:

- No smoke entry: no boot-path file changes; the harness boot stamps against the fake agent at 2.1.287, unaffected
  (a met prompt never occurs there).
- No mutation run (directive item 7).
- No live start reads verify's new line: P0 keeps the prompt off `L1` (directive item 4).

Waits and kills: the new `cli_verify` case drives verify under its binary's 20 s ci kill; the rehearsals wait on the
rig's exit through the file's `run` / `finished` helpers; the rig's `--deadline` bounds each live start below its
entry's `timeout`. No new test sleeps.

Test homes: every new test and rehearsal runs under its own case dirs; `L2` under the rig's scratch at
`/tmp/viola-rig-<uid>/`; only `L1` runs under the founder's real home and config, by his answer 1.

The live legs' non-priming probes are the round entries ahead of them: the install read by path, the rig's census,
`df`, the builds with their hashes, and P0. None primes anything.
**The remove-the-guard control** is implement's one-shot `gate.py control`, not an entry (validation.md check 4 (6)):

- **Id and case:** `bt-line`, in `src/cmd/verify.rs`: the edit removes the statement that writes `BROWSER_TOOLS_STOOD`
  (step 2). The case is `verify_meeting_the_browser_tools_prompt_says_so_before_the_summary`, named as nextest prints
  the NAME.

- **Firing:** on entry 5 with `--timeout 600`; the entry is filtered to the `cli_verify` and `cli_send` binaries and
  runs under the harness's nextest `ci` profile, `fail-fast = false` (`.config/nextest.toml:1-3`), so the named case
  runs whatever its neighbours do. The case alone takes about the verify
  floor, under its 20 s kill.

- **Reading:** «holds» only when that named case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line; a `timeout` reading is not
  «holds», nor is an entry merely red.

live start.

     at the test's end, so a red firing keeps nothing to read today. In that one case, each `box-text` assert's
     message carries the rig summary (`stdout(&out)`: `box`, `keys`, `settle-ms`, `frames`) and the text of the kept
     frame named `after-del` under the case's `--out` (read before the `TempDir` drops; the frames are the rig's own
     local frames, security · decision/live-session-screens-kept-local). No oracle changes.
18b. **The red read before any mend:** implement fires entry 7 (the counted entry, the whole `rig_rehearsal` binary,
     up to 30 firings, stopping at the first red) on the instrumented tree, and names the cause from the red run's
     printed summary and `after-del` frame, recorded in `evidence/r1-red.md`.
     - **Cause A — the rig read the screen before the redraw after DEL settled** (the `after-del` frame shows the box
       without its prompt row, or the settle after the key ended on its quiet window with the redraw still to come):
       the mend is step 18c.
     - **Any other cause shown**, or **no red in the 30 firings** (the cause unread): implement STOPS before the live
       round and says so (`inputs#I3` item 3); it is not chased further in this chunk.
18c. **The mend (Cause A only), `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`:** in `r1_keys`, the settle after `X` and after
     `DEL` waits for a frame whose box is up AND whose prompt row is readable (`r.is_box_up() && r.box_text !=
     "absent"`), bounded by `plan.settle` as now, in place of `|_| true`; the `box-text` word is read from that
     frame. A settle that ends on its bound with no such frame still records what it read (`absent`), so the case
     can still fail.
18d. **The mended reading, a count:** entry 7 fired once after 18c reads green: the `rig_rehearsal` binary run 30
     times in a row, each green. The case that fails without the fix is that same count on the unmended tree:
     18b's red.
     - **Why 30** (a forecast to be measured, not a rate): at P5 the red was read 2 times in 36 whole-binary
       firings (entry 6's baseline red at 22:56Z; a 10-firing count all green; this 30-count's baseline red at its
       25th firing, 23:12Z; the P5 trail `gate-2026-11-18-the-live-home-s-re-stamp-and-the-product-re-pin.json`). At
       2 in 36, 30 firings hold at least one red with probability 1 − (34/36)^30 ≈ 0.82: 18b reads the red about
       4 times in 5, and an unmended tree passing 30 of 30 is about 18% likely, so a 30 of 30 after the mend is
       evidence, not proof; the report records the count read, never «fixed» on it alone.

# Implement directive — «The live home's re-stamp and the product re-pin» (chunk 2026-11-18-the-live-home-s-re-stamp-and-the-product-re-pin)

The plan is approved (rev 11). This window is fresh: read the chunk's documents and run dirs from disk first. This
directive is the only file of its folder you read or snap.

## The live cap for THIS chunk (the founder's own answers: «2 + 1 запасной» 2026-11-18T22:18:16Z, «Перевести на 2.1.328» 2026-11-19T06:01:53Z; nothing widens it)

- **TWO base starts on one ledger, on claude 2.1.328 by path: `L1` first (`--cap 1`), then `L2` (`--cap 2`), and ONE
  spare `L1-2`.** `L1`: the 24-row `viola verify` of his REAL `~/.viola` through the `VH` arm from the repository
  root (9 `claude` processes, one at a time). `L2`: one `/context` reading under the rig's PRIVATE config.
- **The spare is spent only on a cause `L1` ITSELF showed**, after its mend lands through a plan revision — never on
  an inference, never in this run. A third base start is the founder's.
- **No byte into any CLI dialog, no key into a modal.** verify types only its own literals into its own runs.
- **Under his real home `L1` writes only what the plan's file lists name** (`~/.viola/ledger/stamps.json`'s 2.1.328
  entry, `~/.viola/bin/<key>/`, what the CLI itself writes); `VH` reads NO credentials file and makes no copy. The
  reads of his real Claude config are the two he allowed and nothing wider: the key NAME
  `claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled` before `L1` (RED on absent: no start), and key names plus the needle
  `viola-probe-absent` around `L1` — names and `present`/`absent` only, no value kept. Nothing under his home is
  removed by hand; a SIGKILL's leftovers are named in the report.
- Each start is ledgered with the clock's time (`date -u`) BEFORE it is made. Before the live round read the host:
  `python3 ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py read --last 15`; on
  CONTENDED, stop and say so — `L1` is not started on a loaded host (a RED `L1` overwrites this morning's green
  2.1.328 stamp).

## Stops

- **The fold (plan steps 18a–18d) comes first:** if the failing rehearsal shows any cause but the rig reading the
  screen too early, or no red comes in 30 runs, STOP before the live round and say so.
- **A RED live entry stops implement BEFORE the operator pass and before any rebuild** (a RED `L1` leaves `L2`
  unfired): report the entry and what the start itself showed, in its own words, and wait.
- **The re-pin stops BEFORE the switch:** in the operator pass, after the pre-CI commit's CI reads green, the
  rollback copy `viola.2026-11-15` and the new `viola.<sha8>` are placed BESIDE the product. The product file
  `~/.local/viola-product/bin/viola` is NOT replaced and this builder is NOT restarted — that is the operator's
  step, outside the chunk.
- A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and say so. On an account-limit
  refusal, stop where you are.
- The rig keeps its frames and records locally; nothing of the operator's status line or config enters a commit.
  Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home.

## On green

Write the chunk report (P4), then run the operator pass in this same window with the `ci.py conclusion` read
(leg=operator) as usual, and land `evidence/operator-pass.md`. Then stop: the wrap is a fresh window's.
Call no scheduled-wake or timer tool.

## 2026-11-18-the-live-home-s-re-stamp-and-the-product-re-pin — Secret Management: 1 row(s)
**Section:** Secret Management
**Change:** ~ decision/live-rig-credentials-copy · except: was «»; now «The VH arm, run under the real home, makes no copy and reads no credentials file.»
**Why:** decision/live-rig-credentials-copy: The plan's expected amendment names this row for the VH arm, which runs under the real home and reads no credentials, so the row's copy-and-expiry rule no longer holds for every start of the rig. — resolved (Q1), PROVISIONAL: delegate the overseer, 2026-11-19: «the two security-plan rows (live-rig-isolated-child, live-rig-credentials-copy) are CONFIRMED as shown, PROVISIONAL until the founder's own word at the epoch boundary»
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-19T07-27-27Z-wrap/

- Crate dependency direction is enforced by manifests: `viola-core` depends on no viola crate; `viola-pty` knows no agent; `viola-hyprland` is the one compositor seam (queries and dispatches only through its closed request set), sync and tokio-free, depending on `viola-core` alone among viola crates; only `viola-agent-claude` knows Claude payload shapes, including those of `claude agents --json` (except, test-only, the live rig in `viola-e2e`, which reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload and the cachedChromeExtensionInstalled key name, never a value, and seeds its private Claude config, and VH, which reads the real config's key names and a needle, never a value, and the fake agent and the rig, which read a config's trust record); among the product crates only `viola-mcp` enables tokio (`rt`), and `viola-channel` lists it optional behind its `tokio` feature (the `TokioClient`), which `viola-mcp` enables; the root bin holds the subcommand dispatch, the run pump and the wheel, all of which consume only normalised events.

The only crate that knows Claude Code (test-only exceptions: the live rig in `viola-e2e` reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload and the cachedChromeExtensionInstalled key name, never a value, and seeds its private Claude config; VH reads the real config's key names and a needle, never a value; the fake agent and the rig read a config's trust record). It parses hook payloads tolerantly and maps each hook to a normalised kind. It maps dialog answers to decision bodies (S3 / S7 / S8) and applies the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip. It resolves the child program (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and holds the Claude-specific half of the CLI version gate: the capability ledger rows (compiled) with their `viola verify` checks, `parse_version`, the stamp merge and `verified` verdict, and the fixture scrub. The gate's spawn is the root bin's `run::version_gate`; the stamps I/O is `viola_state::stamps`. It keeps the vt100 screen signatures (readiness gate), parses, in the pure `agents` module, a `claude agents --json` answer (`parse` into rows or a closed `AgentsFailure`, `oversize` · `malformed`; the read itself is the root bin's `run::agents`), and normalises `prompt-submitted` (removes the long-paste wrapper, then reverses tag escaping; classifies `origin` driver/human/harness). It also holds the resume shapes `viola revive` launches with (`viola verify`'s Run E is the second caller of `resume_args(id, false)`): `PROGRAM` (`claude`), `RESUME_FLAG`, `FORK_SESSION_FLAG`, `is_session_id` (36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18, 23, ASCII hex elsewhere) and `resume_args(id, fork)`; it is the one product home of the two flag literals. It also holds the pure `marketplace` module, `viola plugin install`'s three documents built by `serde_json` (`marketplace_files`; `NAME` the marketplace `viola`, `PLUGIN_REF` `viola@viola`; its `.mcp.json` registers the MCP server `viola`, no hooks). No adapter trait yet: a second agent arrives as a sibling `viola-agent-<name>` crate, at which point the adapter trait is extracted into `viola-core`.

- **`viola-agent-claude`** — the only crate that knows Claude (save the test-only live rig's read of the key names and source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload, never a value, its seeding of its private Claude config, its read of the `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled` key name there, never a value, the rig's VH arm's read of the real config's key names and one needle word, never a value, and the fake agent's and the rig's read of a Claude config file's trust record): hook JSON and `claude agents --json` shapes, dialog answer mapping, the identity strip, child program resolution, the Claude half of the CLI version gate, the capability ledger and the Claude flag literals; does no file I/O and takes no `viola-state`

- Every dependence on an undocumented `claude` behaviour is a capability-ledger row in `viola-agent-claude` with a `viola verify` probe, never an unconditional assumption (except StopFailure, registered with no ledger row and no verify probe); Claude shapes only in `viola-agent-claude` (save the test-only live rig in `viola-e2e`, which reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload, never a value, and seeds its private Claude config and reads its `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled` key name, never a value, and whose VH arm reads the real config's key names and one needle word, never a value, and the test-only fake agent and rig, which read a Claude config file's trust record); Tokio only in `viola-mcp`.
<!-- GENERATED:setup:warnings end -->

- **CLI** — `viola list` (the k9s-style board, six fixed columns and words the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) reuses; as built: uncoloured under `--json`, a piped stdout, `NO_COLOR` (an empty value included) or `TERM=dumb`, else NAME bold, the `DIALOG` word amber with its kind word plain and a wrapped `stale` row dim end to end; on a terminal whose width is known (`viola_pty::host_size()`, never `COLUMNS`) only an unwrapped NAME too long for its column is cut with `...`; the wrapped rows, then, when one `claude agents --json` read lists a session no wrapped row joins, the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` line and one row per unwrapped session (NAME its `sessionId`, `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI); STATUS `idle` / `busy` on a row the read joins, else `unknown`; a failed read prints the board as with no `claude`; and a failed strict-modes check refuses the whole board with exit 21, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`), the `viola send` readback mirror (an unusable `viola send` and an oversize `viola answer` instead exit 2 with their fixed stderr line, `UNUSABLE_TEXT` / `UNUSABLE_RESPONSE`, whatever `--json` says, and no document; a failed `cli` verb's `error: internal error`, exit 1, is with `--json` among the arguments before a `--` the document `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout with stderr empty, while `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` stay silent at the catch site), phraseology verb output (`viola plugin install`: four plain-ASCII stdout lines in one write, no SGR, `viola@viola  written  <dir>` / `run these to add it to Claude Code:` / `  claude plugin marketplace add <dir>` / `  claude plugin install viola@viola`, `<dir>` quoted only where the host's shell would split it; under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"marketplace":"viola","plugin":"viola@viola"}}`; a refused strict-modes check is exit 21 with `viola list`'s home pair on stderr, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, stderr empty), `viola wait` / `viola last` (one static result line on stdout, no spinner; a `wait` woken by an expired dialog hold prints `dialog-expired  <name>  dialog <id>  cursor <n>`, ASCII, no SGR, written once), `viola link` / `viola unlink` (one plain-ASCII stdout line in one write, no SGR, exit 0: `link    <driver> -> <driven>  since <HH:MM:SSZ>`, `link    <driver> -> <driven>  already linked` for a held pair, `unlink  <driver> -> <driven>` whether or not a pair was removed; under `--json` `{"v":1,"ok":{"since":<ts>,"already_linked":<bool>}}` / `{"v":1,"ok":{}}`; a refused strict-modes check of the driven instance is exit 21 with `revive`'s instance pair on stderr naming it, and so is the one `viola send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` make of their instance before any frame (that pair, not the `[/ ]` mirror; no frame and no line written), or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, stderr empty (exit 21's document is `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, `<cause>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`)), `viola verify` step counter (each relied row's step line ends `pass`, `absent` or `fail`, `absent` only on the `browser-tools-prompt` row when no run met the prompt, counted as a pass there alone, and a run that met that prompt prints, after a successful `stamps.json` update and before the summary, one plain ASCII stdout line, no SGR: `the browser-tools prompt stood at start; viola never answers it: answer it once in claude, then run viola verify again`; the trust-record row's ends `pass` or `fail`; no step line, summary or refusal names the config file, the trust record's key or its value), the `viola run` / `viola revive` passthrough (on a verified CLI the start writes the claude CLI's trust record for an untrusted session folder, flag only, so no trust dialog stands and no key is typed, `revive`'s keyed by the recorded directory; the trust step adds no refusal, exit code, hint, `--json` code or terminal byte; nothing printed while the child runs; `viola revive <name> --list` prints one static line per logged session; under `--json` both arms print one stdout document: `--list`'s `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}`, every refusal of the start it shares with `run`, `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` with exit 1, no hint and stderr empty, `<code>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`; a `pump_child` error prints none, the child having held the terminal)

- The hidden capture arm, `hook <event> --capture`, does no obs init and writes no line (a bounded panic-line exemption, obs-plan §10). `viola verify` runs `strict::check_home_tree` on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens: a refused tree is exit 1 with the home pair, no step line, no log and no line; a refused `update_stamps` (`StampsError::StrictModes`, nothing read or written) prints the same pair and exits 1 through its own `process-exit`, which under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` carries `detail:"strict-modes-failed"`; every other refusal past the tree check writes its own code there (`program-not-found`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `version-unreadable`, `unclean-fixture`), a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, and the fixture's `<file>` enters no code. `viola verify`'s trust-record write and removal emit no log line and no span (a refused symlinked, non-regular or foreign file included); the outcome rides only the stamps. The reading of the CLI's browser-tools prompt as a modal adds no log line, span, event or detail code of its own; verify's reading of it (its `absent` step word included) reaches only the ledger stamp and verify's stdout, whose one fixed line on a met prompt is the only record that the prompt stood at start. Each wrapped start of `viola run` and `viola revive` on a verified CLI opens no span for its trust step and writes exactly one INFO `trust-record` line to the run role file, its required `detail` one of a closed set of 16 start words (`trust-record` in the event enum of both the diag-line and the detail-line schema), and the word never refuses the start; no path, key or value of the claude config reaches any line, stamp or summary. A `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`) starts no further spawn, kills and reaps the child it is running, closes every spawn pair it opened (a child of an interactive PTY run killed at the stop closes with `duration_ms` and a `child_exit_status`, the PTY pump's exit code; a print-mode or `--version` probe child killed at the stop is not measured) and ends `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` (a member of the `process-exit` `detail` enum `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes at 19 values); `run`'s version gate observes no stop.

- `viola verify`'s six interactive PTY children (founder-ratified live, 2026-10-05; Run E the founder's own answer to P4 fork 2 of chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows): direct spawns under the R8 strip, output through `MAX_FRAME`; never a byte typed into any dialog — CLI-native (trust, external imports) or the probe's own; a modal start is killed with no key, and a browser-tools prompt standing at start is left for the human to answer once in claude, as verify says before its summary; a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM is killed with no key, pastes nothing more, and no later run starts; once Run B's first turn has settled, before its framing pastes, Run B makes ONE bounded `claude agents --json` read (Run B's program, the probe dir as cwd, the R8 strip, `VERSION_DEADLINE`, none once a stop is read; held in memory, never written to the captures dir; `--record` keeps only Run B's own row in `Agents.recorded-1.json`, through the scrub; no live start added; the founder's own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board); Run B's seven pastes are compiled literals (the probe prompt, a long text, a tag-like text, a newline text, `/compact`, `/clear`, and seventh `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent`, the local-command-echo relied row's probe, whose write to the user's real Claude config stays unmeasured and which adds one input-history line, accepted residuals of a ratified widening), each added one only into a settled input box (read up only on compiled literals — a footer literal, or a rule row of at least 40 rule chars directly above a row opening the prompt char — and never while a modal literal stands; the one predicate that also decides `viola run`'s pre-send gate), waited for up to the probe deadline (the founder's live answers, 2026-10-06; the newline paste his own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row; the `/compact` paste his own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row, adding no run, start or spawn pair); Runs C and D's dialogs are answered only by the hidden `hook --capture --answers` arm (a `take(64)` closed `ProbeAnswer` id → one `decision_body` on stdout, nothing on any failure, exit 0); Run C's one `allow` runs `touch viola-probe-permission` inside its own dir; Run D's `plansDirectory` is a 0700 `plans/` inside its own dir; Run E runs last with empty input (no key typed) and no `--settings`, its one `--resume <id>` built by `resume_args(id, false)` from the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture only when `is_session_id` accepts it (`ledger::resume_target`; with none it spawns nothing); Run A's OS-temp dir and `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`, `-dialogs/`, `-plan/`, `-resume/` are 0700 and removed when verify passes, fails or is stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`; each guard removes only what that run created); SIGKILL, a crash and a failed handler install leave them, and verify's own trust record in the Claude config, to be removed by hand; viola writes nothing under `~/.claude` save verify's own trust record for its fresh temp folder in the Claude config its child reads, only that record removed after, and the trust flag `run` and `revive`'s start set for an untrusted spawn folder, which stays (the CLI's own Run B / C / D transcripts are the accepted residual, and so is the print-mode probe's empty project dir for its cwd `ledger/probes/<pid>/` under `~/.claude/projects/` (a `memory/` dir, no transcript; the founder's own word, live, 2026-10-19); Run E adds no transcript file). The `--record` refusal names the fixture file and a closed code (`home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`), never the content, and so does the test-only `viola-mcp-tap`'s `fixture` step for the `Mcp.<variant>.json` class (the same scrub, through `ledger::screen_fault`; its `record` capture a 0600 file in a private directory, never committed, its `viola mcp` a direct spawn with no shell and no PATH lookup, the tap started live by the standing rig under its private CLI config); the live rig's MCP recording arm keeps no CLI output (stdout drained and dropped, stderr only as a byte count and a SHA; its MCP config a private 0600 file inside the scratch, removed with it); the test-only `viola-hypr-tap` keeps a reply string only under a closed per-request key allowlist in the form the seam parses (window addresses, the v-digit version tag), every other string the placeholder and a non-JSON reply only `ok`, then the shared scrub runs and an unclean set is refused whole.

- Test homes on the Linux dev host (the founder's live answer, 2026-10-07T07:25Z, relayed by the overseer; a boundary widening): `target/e2e-home` is a link to the per-user tmpfs directory `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>`, so the fixture chain's sweep and drop and harness `cleanup` create and delete outside the working directory, each only a dir the test side itself made (by its owner record, its own temp dir or its session name prefix) or another build's stamp dir whose lock it takes with try_lock. The two keepers follow a linked base only when its target is absolute and one `lstat` reads a real directory with no group or other bit, and refuse a backing whose filesystem reads less than the 9 GiB headroom floor free (`statvfs`), each refusal a fixed message that names no path (the headroom one holds the two counts); they create it 0700 and remove nothing. `viola` never names the backing; no CI runner has the link. Accepted residual (a live round of `viola plugin install`): the round runs the CLI's own four commands (`claude plugin marketplace add` / `install` / `uninstall` / `marketplace remove`) at `--scope local`, a fresh count of four per rig, from a `proj/` that is its own git repo outside this work tree (on the e2e-home tmpfs, no ancestor `CLAUDE.md`): the CLI takes the local scope's project from the git work tree root, and a `proj/` inside the work tree meets the external-imports dialog after the trust dialog; the rig passes the folder-trust dialog by keys into its own pty only, never a desktop key, on the founder's own word anew for each chunk and by a closed argv grant (on a read screen at most 2 arrows toward the trust row and 1 Enter only when that row reads selected, one x and one DEL only in a ready box, any other key writing nothing; the founder's word binds the grant alone, and the rig's stop, Ctrl-C into its own pty or a no-key group kill, needs no word; on a wrapped start the keys move the wheel to the human, and `viola release <name>` precedes the driver's send); the CLI's writes are its own — its trust entry in `~/.claude.json` for each `proj/` whose dialog was accepted, the session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`, and after the removal its orphaned plugin cache `~/.claude/plugins/cache/viola/viola/<version>/` (re-written in place by a later install and uninstall), `installed_plugins.json` and `known_marketplaces.json` back as before (as measured on claude 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings); viola itself writes nothing under `~/.claude` or into `~/.claude.json`, save `viola verify`'s own trust record for its fresh temp folder in the Claude config its child reads, only that record removed after (a SIGKILL leaves it); on a verified CLI only, `run` and `revive`'s start set `hasTrustDialogAccepted` alone (every other key kept) in the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder in the config its child reads, never for the user home folder or a folder the CLI's own walk reads as trusted, and that record stays. Accepted residual (a scratch footer reading of a newer CLI): one `viola run` start of the CLI under a tmpfs `--home`, in a detached 80×24 pane, its cwd a fresh `.viola-footer-<pid>/` under the repository root, with no key typed; one `viola list` read against that home; at two instants the pane's bottom three screen rows, scrubbed of the home and the user word, written to the chunk's `evidence/`, never a row above the footer; then the start is killed and its cwd removed; it left no transcript under `~/.claude/projects/` (as measured on 2.1.302 at chunk 2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows). It is no product path and no standing permission: another such reading needs its own answer. The live rig runs its child under a private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in its own scratch, seeded only with keys whose values come from the CLI bundle's own logic, none read from the user's config (used-config markers and, on every arm but VP, the browser-tools prompt turned off; VP leaves the browser-tools key out), with an environment built from a closed kept list of host names plus its own, and reads the user's `~/.claude.json` only after a moved stamp, searching it for rig-made needles, dropping the bytes and keeping one closed word; the VH arm runs under the real home and config, reads no credentials, keeps only key names and one needle word, prints no value, and needs an explicit home, Claude dir and user config. The live rig may read whether the key name `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled` stands in its own private scratch config, printing written or absent, and never reads a value (a boundary widening, answered for the rig alone). The live rig's MCP recording arm keeps no CLI output (stdout drained and dropped, stderr kept only as a byte count and a SHA), and its MCP config is a private 0600 file inside the scratch, removed with it. The live rig's CX arm reads the session transcript through `MAX_FRAME`, counting only tags past the kept length and keeping no byte of it, and sends only through `viola send` under the rig's private config. A live session's screen frames are kept only under a gitignored local path, never in a work dir, a run dir or a commit; what lands is a closed-word summary per frame. The live rig copies the claude OAuth credentials file owner-only into its private scratch, reads only its expiry, refuses a start with under 20 minutes of token, removes the copy on every exit path, and writes no credential, host path or config value into any ledger, frame or summary; the VH arm, run under the real home, makes no copy and reads no credentials file. The live rig's own UserPromptSubmit capture (a ratified boundary widening) reads the hook payload under `MAX_FRAME` with the default JSON depth and writes one owner-only line of key names matching `[a-z_]{1,40}`, others counted, and one closed source word, never a value; a non-object or over-long payload writes unread.
